transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-07
Time: 15:00 EST
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Ava Martinez (Redwood AE); Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE); Maya Chen (Redwood Solutions); Priya Shah (Silvercrest CISO); Daniel Park (Infra Lead); Sandra Liu (Compliance); Omar Reyes (Network)

Summary:
High-level deep dive on Private (VPC/on-prem) security architecture for Redwood Private deployment. Focus on network isolation, ingress/egress, firewalling, KMS and audit logs. Silvercrest emphasized strict egress controls and SSO/RBAC mapping; asked for SOC2/ISO artifacts and recommended firewall templates. Redwood AE/SE agreed to share docs and a network diagram and proposed next steps for pilot.

Transcript:
[00:00] Ava (Redwood AE): Hey everybody, thanks for taking the time. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Priya (Silvercrest CISO): Priya here.
[00:08] Daniel (Infra): Daniel on my side.
[00:10] Sandra (Compliance): Sandra.
[00:11] Omar (Network): Omar, hi.
[00:12] Liam (Redwood SE): Liam from Redwood engineering.
[00:15] Ava: Great. We'll do a brief agenda: security posture, VPC network isolation, ingress/egress patterns, firewall rules, KMS/encryption, and audit/logging. Then Q&A and next steps. Sound good?
[00:26] Priya: Yep that's good. We are particularly concerned about egress and data residency, and we want the on-prem variant to appear as isolated as possible.
[00:36] Liam: Great. I'll start with the high-level architecture. For Redwood Private we provide a control plane you can host in your VPC or on-prem; the inference runtime sits in customer-managed subnets. Ingress is over TLS to a secured load balancer; egress is restricted and can be proxied through customer egress proxies. We also support a fully air-gapped mode for on-prem if needed.
[00:58] Daniel: When you say control plane, is that still contacting Redwood-hosted services or is it entirely customer-managed for Private?
[01:05] Ava: Good q. For Private you have a choice: a managed control plane that talks to Redwood endpoints over a peered connection, or a customer-hosted control plane where no management plane traffic leaves your network. For the latter, Redwood provides deployable manifests and scripts.
[01:23] Omar: If we go customer-hosted control plane, how does upgrade telemetry work? We need to ensure no telemetry crosses our outbound egress without our explicit permission.
[01:34] Liam: In the customer-hosted mode, telemetry is opt-in. We provide a telemetry collector that can be disabled; logs can be forwarded to your SIEM instead. The default is to not exfil any PII; only basic health pings are available and those are configurable.
[01:49] Sandra: On audit logs, can we get full request/response logs or just metadata? Our compliance team requires request IDs, timestamps, user IDs, and audit trails for admin actions.
[02:01] Maya (Redwood Solutions): We typically surface detailed admin audit logs (who changed config, rollouts, API key actions) and request metadata. We do not store raw customer prompt content in the control plane unless configured; for the inference plane you can choose to disable request logging or send logs to your own S3/GCS endpoint.
[02:20] Priya: Important for us: we need audit logs to land in our Splunk instance, with retention of 7 years. Is that supported?
[02:28] Liam: Yes, we support pushing logs to Splunk via HEC, or to your SIEM via syslog/secure forwarder. Retention policies are controlled by you. We provide formatted JSON events that include request_id, model, timestamp, route, and user.
[02:44] Daniel: Regarding ingress, does Redwood support private link or VPC peering for the control plane?
[02:50] Ava: We support VPC peering, PrivateLink (for AWS), and direct on-prem connectors. For sensitive accounts we recommend PrivateLink if you're on AWS because it keeps traffic off the public internet.
[03:02] Omar: We operate through a corporate proxy for all outbound egress. Can Redwood runtime be configured to route egress via our proxy?
[03:10] Liam: Absolutely. The runtime allows configuring an egress proxy (HTTP(S) proxy) and supports proxy authentication. Egress to external repos or telemetry is blocked unless routed through your proxy.
[03:20] Priya: On encryption - how are keys managed? We want KMS integration and customer-managed key support with key rotation policies.
[03:28] Liam: We integrate with cloud KMS services (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) and can also integrate with customer HSMs via KMIP. In Private mode you can supply keys; Redwood never holds plaintext keys. We support envelope encryption for model weights at rest and TLS in transit. Key rotation is supported and we have recommended procedures for re-encrypting persisted caches.
[03:49] Sandra: Do you support BYOK where we retain ultimate control and Redwood accesses keys only via transient grants?
[03:55] Maya: Yes, BYOK is supported for encryption at rest. For decryption at runtime you can do either: give the runtime permission via an IAM role with a KMS grant, or use a proxy HSM where the key is never directly exportable.
[04:08] Daniel: A lot of our infra is behind strict egress filters. Will the inference containers need to pull from external registries at runtime?
[04:16] Liam: No. Images can be pre-pulled into your private registry (ECR/GCR/ACR) and the runtime will use those. We provide an image bundle you can import. If you prefer, the runtime can be built from a local artifact so it never contacts public registries post-deploy.
[04:32] Omar: For firewalling, where do you recommend placing IDS/IPS sensors? Pre-ingress or post-ingress? Do you have recommended rule sets?
[04:41] Liam: Best practice is to have an external perimeter firewall that handles public ingress to the load balancer, and then an internal micro-segmentation layer - security groups and host-level firewall rules - around the runtime nodes. IDS/IPS typically sits at the north-south boundary and also as an east-west sensor between subnets, because you want to catch lateral movement. We can share a recommended baseline rule set.
[05:01] Priya: If we require zero public egress from the inference nodes, can we still push model updates?
[05:07] Ava: Model updates can be delivered via your private pipeline. For example, you can host model artifacts in your internal object store and schedule rollout jobs that point to internal URIs. We support that.
[05:18] Daniel: What about KV cache? Is that stored locally and encrypted? Could that be forwarded out accidentally?
[05:24] Liam: KV cache is stored on local disk and can be encrypted at rest with your KMS keys. It is not sent to Redwood. Any cache snapshot exports are optional and require explicit action.
[05:36] Omar: Concerning egress allowlist, we already have a long list (monitoring, patching, repo). Will Redwood provide a minimal egress allowlist so we can add the exceptions easily to our corporate proxy?
[05:44] Liam: Yes, we'll provide a minimal egress allowlist and DNS names/IP ranges. We recommend locking egress down to only your registries, internal telemetry endpoints, and KMS endpoints where applicable.
[05:55] Priya: On RBAC and SSO, we use SAML SSO and want to map corporate groups to Redwood roles. Is role mapping flexible?
[06:02] Maya: We support SAML and OIDC; group-to-role mapping is configurable. You can map LDAP or SAML group claims to admin, developer, or auditor roles. We also support SCIM for provisioning.
[06:13] Sandra: For compliance, we need separation of duties: who can change rollout policies vs who can read logs. Does Redwood have fine-grained RBAC?
[06:20] Liam: Yes, we have granular RBAC - policy management, model deploy, config changes, read-only audit roles, and a dedicated role for billing. Access changes are recorded in the audit log.
[06:30] Daniel: About network segmentation - do you recommend a dedicated subnet per runtime cluster?
[06:34] Liam: We recommend dedicated subnets per environment (prod/stage) and per cluster in high-security setups so you can apply subnet-level ACLs, routing, and monitoring.
[06:44] Omar: What about egress to cloud provider metadata endpoints - must the runtime access instance metadata to get credentials?
[06:50] Liam: The runtime supports passing credentials via mounted secrets or instance profiles. If you are strict about metadata access, we can use mounted IAM role credentials or short-lived tokens issued via your agent instead of allowing instance metadata calls.
[07:04] Priya: Data residency: we can't move data outside EU. If we deploy in our EU region, are there any control plane calls that go to US endpoints?
[07:12] Ava: For customer-hosted control plane everything stays in your region. For managed control plane we have regionized endpoints and you can require routing to EU-only endpoints. We'll share our region coverage map.
[07:24] Sandra: On encryption in transit, do you support mTLS between internal services?
[07:29] Liam: Yes, mTLS is supported for service-to-service traffic inside the cluster; you can configure cert rotation and supply your CA. We also support verifying client certs for admin APIs.
[07:41] Daniel: Can we integrate with our central secrets manager instead of provider KMS?
[07:45] Maya: If your secrets manager exposes a standard API and can perform KMS-like operations, we can integrate. We also have a pluggable secrets provider interface.
[07:54] Omar: For firewall rules, we use explicit port whitelisting. Which ports does Redwood need open east-west?
[07:59] Liam: Primarily the runtime uses gRPC/tcp on configurable ports - we provide a default 8080/8443 for control plane and 9000+ for intra-node comms. We'll provide an exact port matrix.
[08:11] Priya: What about image signing and supply chain? We need attestation that the images haven't been tampered with.
[08:17] Liam: We support signed image bundles and can verify signatures at deploy time. We also integrate with COSIGN and supply SBOMs per release.
[08:26] Sandra: For audit reqs, we need immutable logs. Can logs be push-only to our append-only store?
[08:32] Maya: Yes, you can configure logs to be pushed to your append-only S3 with immutability policies, or to an on-prem WORM storage.
[08:40] Daniel: If we set egress to zero, is there any periodic licensing/heartbeat needed to keep features enabled?
[08:48] Ava: No heartbeat is required for customer-hosted control plane; licensing is handled via the license file you install. For managed control plane there is periodic check-in but it can be done over PrivateLink.
[08:59] Omar: How does Redwood handle CVE patches for the runtime? Do you recommend a canary first in an isolated subnet?
[09:06] Liam: Best practice: push a canary to an isolated subnet and run smoke tests. We provide upgrade playbooks and an automated canary rollout strategy.
[09:18] Priya: Okay quick question on backups - if KV caches are encrypted, what about backups of model artifacts, any recommended encryption policies?
[09:25] Liam: Model artifacts should be stored in an encrypted object store with server-side or client-side encryption. We recommend server-side encryption with your KMS keys and lifecycle policies that align with your retention rules.
[09:36] Daniel: For the pilot, we plan to spin up a small cluster in our staging VPC. We'll need a network diagram from Redwood to compare against our topology.
[09:44] Ava: We'll provide a recommended staging VPC diagram and suggested security group/ACL settings.
[09:49] Sandra: For compliance review, will you provide a SOC 2 Type II attestation and the associated control descriptions?
[09:55] Ava: Yes, we will share SOC 2 Type II and ISO27001 certificates, plus control mapping docs. Note some artifacts are redacted but we can run an NDA if needed for deeper artifacts.
[10:06] Priya: We will want an NDA and then ask for the detailed test results.
[10:10] Ava: Understood, we can coordinate with legal.
[10:13] Liam: A little bit more on firewalling specifics: for egress we recommend only allowing DNS to your resolver and HTTPS to your registry and KMS endpoints. All else should be blocked and go through a proxy which can perform TLS inspection. For east-west, keep microsegmentation to limit lateral spread.
[10:32] Omar: Do you have support for IP allowlists and naming conventions for nodes so we can detect suspicious traffic?
[10:37] Liam: Yes we can publish stable internal DNS names and label nodes. We'll also export node metadata into your monitoring system so you can tie flows to instances.
[10:46] Sandra: On data retention, we need to enforce deletion of logs and prompts after X days. Does Redwood have built-in retention configs?
[10:53] Maya: Yes, retention windows for different class of logs can be configured per-tenant: audit logs, request metadata, and debug traces each have independent TTLs.
[11:02] Daniel: Are there any third-party components in the runtime that we should be aware of for SBOM?
[11:07] Liam: We produce an SBOM with every release listing third-party components and licenses.
[11:12] Priya: For SSO, we need SCIM sync to disable accounts on offboarding. Is SCIM bi-directional?
[11:18] Maya: We support inbound SCIM provisioning and group sync; user deprovisioning is handled via SCIM or via your IdP deactivation flows.
[11:25] Omar: Can the runtime be deployed air-gapped and still accept model updates via physical transfer?
[11:30] Liam: Yes, we support air-gapped workflows where you import signed bundles via a USB or secure transfer into your internal registry.
[11:36] Priya: Any concerns about GPU telemetry? We want zero telemetry about the prompts, but anonymized perf metrics are OK.
[11:44] Liam: We can restrict telemetry to anonymized perf counters only, and that's opt-in. No prompt content is collected unless you enable request logging.
[11:53] Sandra: For encryption key rotation - if we rotate keys, how do you recommend handling existing cached artifacts?
[11:59] Liam: You would re-encrypt caches during a rolling maintenance window; we provide tooling to decrypt and re-encrypt cached shards with the new key in a controlled way.
[12:12] Ava: We're near the end - quick recap and next steps. Ava speaking: Redwood to share SOC2/ISO artifacts (Ava); Liam to share VPC diagram and egress allowlist and firewall template (Liam); Silvercrest to share current network topology and proxy lists (Daniel). Also coordinate legal NDA for detailed artifacts.
[12:32] Priya: Sounds good. We'll start the NDA.
[12:34] Daniel: We'll get the topology to you by Friday.
[12:36] Sandra: Compliance will review once we get the artifacts.
[12:38] Ava: Great, thanks everyone. We'll follow up in email and drop the docs into the CRM.

Action items (recap):
- Ava: Share SOC2/ISO artifacts and compliance pack (due 2026-12-09)
- Liam: Send VPC network diagram, ports matrix, and minimal egress allowlist (due 2026-12-11)
- Daniel: Share network topology and proxy egress list (due 2026-12-10)

References mentioned:
- SOC 2 Type II, ISO27001 certs (will share under NDA)
- Image signing (COSIGN), SBOMs per release
- Splunk HEC integration for audit logs

End of transcript.
